_what: Which committed receipt each card replays (cards, by device name) and which an unlisted card of a recorded architecture replays (architectures, "major.minor"). Read by this fixture's parity tests and by tools/advect_wrf471_oracle/recapture_receipt.py, which adds a card here when it installs that card's first capture. uncertified_stale records, per receipt of an architecture older than Blackwell, the commit that left its pins behind and those pins: byte identity is certified on Blackwell and newer only (ruling 2026-10-04), so such a receipt is reported, not gated, and recapture_receipt.py --install drops its record. certified_stand_in records a receipt of an older architecture that gates exactly as a certified one, standing in for a certified receipt recorded as not re-pinned (user ruling 2026-11-17: the sm_120 receipt can be re-recorded only on an RTX 5090; the RTX A6000 receipt verifies kernel edits meanwhile); recapture_receipt.py --install of the certified receipt drops both records.

gpu-receipt-sm86.json.reason: user ruling 2026-11-17: the RTX 5090 receipt can be re-recorded only on an RTX 5090, which no lane can reach; the RTX A6000 (sm_86, pb) is recorded and verified in its place, so a kernel edit here moves this receipt only through a capture on the A6000 that reproduces every production word

gpu-receipt-sm120.json.reason: zero_first (advection.cu, pd_advection.cu) moved the source; no Blackwell card was available to recapture (decision 2026-11-14). tests/test_advection_zero_first.py holds zero_first word-identical to fill-then-accumulate on CUDA and Metal; STALE pending a re-record on an RTX 5090 (only that card can re-record it, user 2026-11-17): gpu-receipt-sm86.json (RTX A6000) gates kernel edits meanwhile
